item.title: Twin Falls loop, 7 miles — Wed Nov 4, 8:45 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **Twin Falls Loop** Mileage: approx 7 miles Elevation gain: 800’ Difficultly: moderate Speed: 2-2.5 mph
We’ll meet at the Pisgah Ranger station at 8:45 for a 9:00 sharp departure. We’ll car pool to the Buckhorn Gap trailhead. The hike will start on Buckhorn Gap, turn onto Avery Creek trail to Clawhammer. Head up Clawhammer to Clawhammer road and back up to Buckhorn Gap. Coming down Buckhorn Gap we will turn onto the Twin Falls trail, stopping at the falls for lunch/snack. Return to Buckhorn Gap trailhead and back to the cars.
If you would rather meet at the trailhead please let a comment. We should be starting the hike at 9:15 from the trailhead.
Dogs are welcome. I will have my dog with me.
Source: Asheville Hiking Group

item.description:

This is a fresh approach to them—a way to quit working on the same old problems and start outgrowing them.

Your first dance partner is yourself.
The second is the floor. But between those two; an infinite array of partners: your body - its joints, tendons, muscles... your mind - its thoughts, memories, imaginings...
And beyond that, the music... another dancer... Third... fourth.. beyond!
Start from that first... work with each partner... listen deeply, and find your way to an integrated ensemble.

item.title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum — Sat Dec 5, 9:30 AM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. Join Joshua on 8/22, 10/3, 11/7, and 12/5. Joshua Cant
